h1: Davos ski resort, stays & events guide
heroText: Davos sits at 1,560 metres, the highest town in the Alps, and it does not have one ski mountain but six: Parsenn, Jakobshorn, Schatzalp-Strela, Madrisa, Pischa and Rinerhorn. Together they hold 300 kilometres of snow-sure slopes served by 57 transport systems. Parsenn alone has around 97 kilometres; the Jakobshorn has 55 from blue to black, and carries the JatzPark at around 2,500 metres.
stayOverview: Davos Platz and Davos Dorf sit at either end of the same street, each with its own railway station and its own lift: the Parsennbahn from Dorf, the Jakobshorn cable car from Platz. Klosters is over the Parsenn on the other side.
hotelIntro: Book against high season. Platz and Dorf each put you at the foot of a different mountain; Klosters is the quieter end of the same ski area.
rentalCars: Davos is reached by the Rhaetian Railway through the Prättigau, about two and a half hours from Zurich.

season.unannounced: No season dates are published on the operator’s snowsports page, its mountains overview or the Parsenn and Jakobshorn pages.

pistes.value: 253 km across five mountains, on 81 runs
pistes.note: The lift company's own count. The destination site davos.ch says 300 km across six mountains; we follow the lift company, which operates them.

baseElevation.unannounced: The lift company's facts page counts slopes, runs, lifts and freeride runs, and its Parsenn page gives the 2,844 m summit, but neither states a base altitude for the ski area.
baseElevation.sourceLabel: Davos Klosters Bergbahnen: facts and figures

longestRun.note: Parsenn is the biggest of the five areas, with some 97 km of slopes and a summit at 2,844 m on the Weissfluh.

dayPass.note: One day on the regional pass covering all five mountains, for adults from 18. A Parsenn and Jakobshorn day pass is CHF 87 and Rinerhorn CHF 69. The lift company says prices are subject to change and publishes its low and high-season lists separately.
